title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
layout_note: Overview at the top: a bottom-up pyramid on the left and a top-down pyramid on the right, joined level by level by horizontal lateral arrows; a dashed zoom box on one right-hand level opens into a large dashed detail frame below.
grouping: No containers in the overview; the two pyramids are grouped by position (left column, right column). A small dashed rectangle on the middle right plane is tied by two dashed grey lines to a large dashed frame below that holds the building block.
shapes_depth: Every feature level is an outlined, unfilled parallelogram in oblique perspective; the left pyramid's planes shrink upward and their outline weight grows from thin light cyan at the bottom to heavy cyan at the top, while every right-pyramid plane is heavy cyan. The input photo is a faded plane with an orange outline at the bottom left. Outputs are small square-cornered 'predict' boxes. The detail panel is flat: two square boxes ('1x1 conv', '2x up'), a circled plus, black arrows.
proposed_highlight: The paper's addition (the top-down pathway with lateral connections) is the right-hand pyramid, drawn with uniformly heavy outlines, and its merge step is expanded into the dashed zoom panel below.
lesson: Encode feature strength as outline weight on the pyramid planes, and zoom one lateral merge into a dashed detail frame tied to it by dashed leader lines.

arrangement.units: One overview (two pyramids side by side, predict boxes at the right) above a dashed detail frame for the merge block; the detail is linked by dashed leader lines, not set off as a separate titled panel.
arrangement.inputs_as: a faded real photo as the lowest, orange-outlined plane of the left pyramid
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn ('predict' boxes at each right-hand level)
arrangement.shared: none drawn (the caption-level fact that heads are shared across levels is not shown)

taxonomy.task: multi-scale feature pyramid for object detection

insights.structure: A shrinking bottom-up pyramid of planes sits on the left, a top-down pyramid of equal levels on the right, joined by one horizontal arrow per level, with a dashed detail frame for the merge block placed underneath.
insights.data: Feature levels are unfilled oblique planes whose outline weight grows with depth on the left, the input is a faded photo as the lowest plane, and outputs are small 'predict' text boxes.
insights.emphasis: The new top-down pathway is the uniformly heavy-outlined right pyramid, and its lateral merge is enlarged in a dashed zoom frame showing '1x1 conv', '2x up' and a circled plus.
insights.flow: Read up the left pyramid on short arrows, across on lateral arrows, down the right pyramid, then right to 'predict'; in the zoom, the lateral input enters from the left and the upsampled input from the top.
insights.avoid: The overview has no labels at all (no stage names, no scales), so the meaning of outline weight and the two pyramids is left entirely to the caption.

notes: Venue written as arXiv: CVPR 2017 is remembered, not printed on the first page. year = arXiv preprint year (1612.03144). The input photo on the lowest plane is a faded image. Fig. 1 (four schemes for multi-scale features, (a)-(d), with FPN as (d)) is the paper's well-known comparison figure and could be carded as a side-by-side-comparison companion.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
